skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2, right after introductions, the interviewer stated the Committee and company are the only clients, that they do not represent the witness personally, are not his attorney, and cannot give him legal advice, and asked whether he had questions.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer said the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and may disclose what is learned, including to the government, without the witness's consent.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: At T6 the interviewer explained the structure of the interview, asked for complete answers, set speculation and estimate ground rules, and asked the witness to say whether he remembered or was reconstructing. The tone stayed professional throughout.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: At T4 the interviewer asked the witness to restate in his own words who was represented and who controls privilege, and the witness answered correctly at T5. The check was effective, though the interviewer did not revisit whether the witness had questions after that.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: At T64 and T66 the interviewer asked whether anything was missing and who else to speak with. At T68 they gave a confidentiality reminder, a document-retention instruction, a no-contact-with-witnesses instruction, and a note that they may follow up. The witness was not asked directly whether there was 'nothing else' beyond T65.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
This interview is confidential and privileged, but that privilege belongs to the company, not to you or to us.
Before we go on, could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
You represent the company. The company controls the privilege. Can we move on?
Please give me complete answers, even if a detail seems minor.
Throughout, please tell me whether you actually remember something or are reconstructing it, and say so if you're unsure.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: The open invitation at T14 ('Tell me everything you remember') was good, but the rest of the interview relied on narrow questions such as 'Who raised it with them first?' and 'How much did it receive?', so the witness rarely walked through events in his own words.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moved from role (T8) to the open LJM1 question (T14) and then to specific points such as who raised the GP role. Later it moved from the Board presentation to Southampton and then to Chewco, in a reasonable order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were short and clear. Some were compound, such as T42 'Did you tell the Board, Mr. Lay, or Mr. Skilling about the Foundation's investment?', and T56 presupposed the answer by asking how he knew reviews occurred.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stayed polite and in control. T40 was firm but fair ('How does that fit with what you told the Board about not receiving value from the Enron stock?'), and the interviewer did not argue with the witness's terse answers.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer changed approach when the witness deflected, pinning him down at T42 to T45 and asking for the disclosure considerations at T50 after the vague answer at T49. They did not pursue the minutes claim at T25 or the approval sheets, so adaptation was partial.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Let's start with your role. As CFO, what were you responsible for?
Did you tell the Board, Mr. Lay, or Mr. Skilling about the Foundation's investment?
How does that fit with what you told the Board about not receiving value from the Enron stock?
So that I have it right: none of them was told?
How do you know Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy reviewed every LJM2 deal?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer confronted the gap between the witness's Board statement and the Foundation's $4.5 million at T38 and T40, and followed the 'It didn't come up' answer at T42 to T45. The interviewer did not challenge 'It's in the minutes' at T25 or the controls answers at T57 to T59.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked who raised the GP role and how much the Foundation received, but rarely established dates, sequences, or who decided Chewco's structure and when.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: After the witness said 'I'd have to check' at T37, the interviewer supplied the approximate figure at T38. The minutes were shown at T52 for recognition. No other memory-refreshing approaches were tried.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer separated personal knowledge from secondhand knowledge. They asked whether the witness had checked the controls (T58, 'Not personally') and how he knew the reviews occurred (T56), and at T44 confirmed that none of the Board, Lay or Skilling was told by the witness.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: At T66 the interviewer asked who else to speak with, and the witness named Causey, Buy and Kopper. The interviewer did not probe Glisan, Mordaunt or the other Southampton investors, though the witness referred to Glisan earlier at T13 and T29.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked about approval sheets signed after closing (T60 to T63) and showed the November 5, 1997 minutes at T52, but did not ask for the sheets or for documents tied to the Southampton investment. Documents were requested only generically at T68.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: At T24 the interviewer asked 'How sure are you that's what you told them?' and at T58 asked whether the witness had checked the controls. These tested how certain the witness was about specific facts.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed up on several material answers: 'Several million' at T38, 'It didn't come up' at T42 to T45, and 'There were disclosure considerations' at T49 to T51. Other material answers, such as 'Raptor I, maybe others' at T63, were not followed up.

moments.text: Who raised it with them first?
How sure are you that's what you told them?
How much did it receive?
Our information is roughly $4.5 million, about six weeks after it invested. Does that fit your memory?
So that I have it right: none of them was told?
What were those disclosure considerations?
Did you check that it was followed?
Who else should we speak with?
Raptor I, maybe others. The sheets would show it.
Witness says the Board statement is in the minutes; the interviewer did not test that claim against the minutes.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The minutes were shown at T52 with a recognition question, which partly authenticated them. They were not introduced by first asking what the witness remembered about the November 5, 1997 meeting or about the Chewco structure.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The Chewco questions at T46 to T51 were asked before the minutes were shown, so the witness's account was partly drawn out first. The interviewer did not ask what he remembered about the November 5 meeting before showing the document at T52.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The interviewer did not describe the minutes to the witness at all. The only description was the question at T54 about whether they mention Kopper's role, which was not a description of the document.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The interviewer did not draw conclusions from the minutes after showing them. The question at T54 asked the witness what the document says without stating an inference.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: After the witness answered 'No' at T55 about Kopper's role in the minutes, the interviewer moved on without inviting him to explain any difference between the minutes and the Chewco account he had given.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
They look like the Committee's minutes.
Do they mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?
No.
The Chewco questions at T46 to T51 were asked before the minutes were shown, so the witness's account was partly drawn out first.

missed_opportunities: T51: The witness said that if a senior officer were involved it would have to be in the proxy. This is a material admission about why Kopper was substituted, and the interviewer did not ask who decided the substitution or why.
T63: The witness said approval sheets were sometimes signed after a deal closed and named Raptor I, maybe others. The interviewer did not ask which sheets, when they were signed, or request them.
tips: When you said that if a senior officer were involved it would have to be in the proxy, who decided that Michael Kopper rather than you would manage Chewco, and when was that decided?
Before I show you the minutes, what do you remember about the November 5, 1997 meeting, who was on the call, and what was said about Michael Kopper's role?
